svg.title: Gear ratio: motor turns per wheel turn
svg.desc: Animated. A motor, seen end-on, drives a wheel through gears. The motor spins five and a half times while the wheel turns once, and two counter bars fill together: 5.5 motor turns for 1 wheel turn, the 5.50:1 of a MAXSwerve drive with a 12T pinion. A table lists 12T 5.50:1, 13T 5.08:1 and 14T 4.71:1. Below, two modules drive straight the same real distance: one with a 12T pinion and one built with a 14T pinion, both with the code saying 5.50; the second reports less. If the code's number is wrong, every distance and speed is wrong by the same factor. MAXSwerve drive is 3 times spur over pinion.
svg.text: Gear ratio: motor turns per wheel turn
MAXSwerve drive with a 12T pinion is 5.50:1: 5.5 motor turns for every wheel turn.
Driving straight, every module should report the same distance.
Bars: the distance each reports. Dashed: the real distance.
If the code's number is wrong, every distance and speed is wrong
by the same factor. MAXSwerve drive is 3 × spur / pinion.
